results.title: AI returns malformed JSON
results.detail: status=error attempts=3 finalize=0 — no Completed session created

events: 1788972721.449 fail: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)

findings: malformed JSON consumed 3 attempts. processor.py's own comment classifies a 'malformed AI response' as Permanent, but r.json() is parsed OUTSIDE call_ai's try block, so it falls to loop()'s generic `except Exception` and is retried as transient.

results.title: AI returns valid JSON with missing/partial fields
results.detail: missing-segments → error in 1 attempt (rejected, not stored); empty-text → no_text=True, recording=None

results.title: Out-of-order status updates or late responses
results.detail: lost-response replay: finalize called 2x, recordings created=1, terminal=done; duplicate rejected as already_linked=True

events: 1788972730.843 finalize applied server-side, then answered 500 — response lost
1788972731.860 LATE/DUPLICATE finalize -> already_linked, no second recording

findings: a finalize whose RESPONSE was lost leaves the row already finalized, yet the worker still calls requeue_session() — the job returns to `queued` and is processed again (a second paid AI call and a second recordings-bucket copy). No duplicate reaches the user because finalize-session's recording_id guard catches it, but the terminal state IS regressed. Whether requeue_session() itself refuses to move a `done` row could not be verified: the async_processor_state_machine migration SQL is not checked into the repo.

results.title: Session metadata, timestamp, time-zone, device association
Time zone, DST transition, device clock skew
results.detail: the upload API carries NO client timestamp — created_at is the database's own UTC default, so a wrong recorder clock cannot skew stored time (observed skew 36s). DST is not representable: storage is UTC throughout.
